thread.title: Scoot over, pork pies — quiche is now in Britain’s inflation-tracking goods basket - MarketWatch

author: Carla Mozee
title: Scoot over, pork pies — quiche is now in Britain’s inflation-tracking goods basket - MarketWatch
text:
Getty Images A royal chef prepares mini-quiches of wilted spring onion and watercress at Buckingham Palace. Sorry, pork pies, but the U.K.’s love of quiche has proved strong enough to bump the traditional British dish from the country’s gauge of inflation in favor of one with French origins.
And perhaps because Britons have been busy exercising off that quiche consumption, gym leggings were added to U.K.’s price-inflation basket of goods and services for 2018, while lager sales at nightclubs was tossed out.
The changes, outlined Tuesday, are part of an annual review by the Office for National Statistics of changing habits among British consumers and subsequent revisions of the so-called shopping basket.
“Quiche has been introduced to improve coverage of the pizza and quiche subclass within bread and cereals,” the ONS said in its statement.
As well as introducing items to represent distinct sectors or markets, the ONS widens out the range of products for established groupings where spending is usually significant.
With that in mind, “prepared, chilled mashed potato” was added because that dish has been popping up on store shelves alongside frozen chips — a.k.a. fries. Women’s exercise leggings improves coverage of the recreational and sports clothing group, and body moisturizing lotion was tossed in to further represent the body care market, said the ONS.
Action cameras and a digital media player, such as Apple Inc.’s AAPL, -0.30% Apple TV AAPL, -0.30% and Amazon’s AMZN, -0.26% Fire TV, also made the new list, but at the expense of the digital television recorder.
Also out of the 2018 shopping basket: leg waxing, ATM charges, Edam cheese and Britain’s famous pork pies. “In each case, it is judged that price changes for these items remain adequately represented by others that remain in the baskets,” said the ONS.
Sales of lager at nightclubs was said to have been removed alongside a fall in the number of nightclubs in the U.K.
Last year, gin was among the items added to the inflation basket, owing to a boom in British sales in recent years.
